texts.q0.q: Oizumi Town (大泉町) was formed in Showa 32 by a merger of Okawa Village (大川村) and which other municipality?
texts.q0.why: In Showa 32 (1957), Okawa Village (大川村) and Koizumi Town (小泉町) merged to become Oizumi Town (大泉町).
texts.q1.q: In which month, in the last third of the month, is the Oizumi Festival (大泉まつり) held every year?
texts.q1.why: The Oizumi Festival (大泉まつり) is held every year in late September, with Prefectural Route 142 (県道142号) closed to cars and open only to pedestrians.
texts.q2.q: The spring "town flower" of Oizumi Town (大泉町) is the tulip. What is the autumn one?
texts.q2.why: The town flowers are officially set as the tulip for spring and the salvia for autumn.
texts.q3.q: Jonouchi Park (城之内公園) was developed on part of what?
texts.q3.a: The main bailey (本丸) and second bailey (二の丸) of Koizumi Castle (小泉城)
texts.q3.b: The main keep (天守) of Okawa Castle (大川城)
texts.q3.c: The third bailey (三の丸) of Tatebayashi Castle (館林城)
texts.q3.why: Jonouchi Park (城之内公園) was developed on part of the main bailey (本丸) and second bailey (二の丸) of Koizumi Castle (小泉城), and it is a famous spot for cherry blossoms.

texts.i0: Oizumi Town (大泉町) was formed in Showa 32 (1957) through the merger of Okawa Village (大川村) and Koizumi Town (小泉町).
texts.i1: Jonouchi Park (城之内公園) (2-chome 24, Jonouchi / 城之内2丁目24番) was developed on part of the main enclosure and second enclosure of Koizumi Castle (小泉城), and is a famous cherry blossom spot.
texts.i2: Every year in late September, the "Oizumi Festival" (大泉まつり) is held. Prefectural Route 142 (県道142号) is closed to vehicles and becomes a pedestrian zone, with festival floats, portable shrines, an International Stage (インターナショナルステージ), and more.
texts.i3: The town flowers are the tulip (spring) and the salvia (autumn), and the symbol tree is the zelkova.

texts.m1.person: People who live in areas expected to be flooded
texts.m1.wall: They do not know where or when to evacuate
texts.m1.why: About 18,730 people live in areas expected to be flooded (44.4% of the town). About 4,370 of them are 65 or older (approximate). It is important to know where the evacuation sites (避難場所) are.
texts.m2.person: Older people who live far from a bus stop
texts.m2.wall: They have few ways to get around
texts.m2.why: 73.9% of people 65 or older live 500 m or more from a bus stop (バス停) (counting only buses with timetable data; approximate). If bus information does not reach them, it becomes hard to get to hospitals and shops.

texts.h0131: In Sengoku (仙石), 88.5% of people live in areas expected to be flooded. There are 4 evacuation sites in the district. First decide with your family where to flee and which route to take, and remember it separately from the evacuation shelter.
texts.h0132: In Oaza Sengoku (大字仙石), 99.7% of people live in areas expected to be flooded. 32.6% are aged 65 or older. During heavy rain, call out to one another early, and check the route to the evacuation site so that you can evacuate together with older people.
texts.h0140: In Oaza Kamikoizumi (大字上小泉), the probability of an earthquake of upper 6 or higher on the Japanese scale in the next 30 years is 5.1%. 67.8% of people live in areas expected to be flooded. texts.h0150: In Oaza Furuumi (大字古海), 81.9% of people live in areas expected to be flooded. There are 3 evacuation sites in the district. Before heavy rain, talk with your family first about where to flee and which route to take.

texts.h0180: In Oaza Yoshida (大字吉田), 96% of people live in areas expected to be flooded. There are 8 evacuation sites in the district. There were 60 personal-injury accidents in 3 years, and 6 involved pedestrians. Please check your evacuation route and stay safe when walking on the road.
